b2_r3: Still, I wouldn't write off genuine feelings about who you're attracted to, or your gender, as "just intrusive thoughts" only because they're confusing or unwanted. Or decide it's "not really me" because the people around you would disapprove (I'm not pushing anyone toward or away from any orientation or gender). Maybe it's been there a long time, and you keep pushing it away. Nobody has to settle that now, and what you do meanwhile can follow what you care about. Over time, what keeps showing up in your actual life tells you more than how often a thought comes back. No single feeling settles it for you, and neither does anyone else, though a good therapist can help you see the pattern.
f1_r3: Anxiety deserves the same kind of listening. It might really be warning you about something, overload maybe, or a boundary someone's about to cross. Being scared of something doesn't make it true, though, even when it feels like it does. I'd ask it what it's worried about and then look at what actually happens, without promising to do what it says. If you always steer around what it fears, you never find out whether it was right. You might find it's been right more than you gave it credit for, or that it cries wolf about the same thing every time. If it might be danger right now, or something in your body a doctor should see, I'd handle that first and check later whether the anxiety was right.
f2_r3: Some of it I wouldn't test at all, even when it sounds like a prediction. If a part hesitates about being touched or about sex, that's enough to stop. And if it says no to going deeper in this work, or to an altered state, I'd stop there too. It might not be able to tell you why.
